posts.body_html:
Hi Victwei! I think I'll be able to get some good photos of clone B this year, we'll see! While I'm fairly certain that clone A originated from Liberty Co, FL, I'm not to sure if clone B is a liberty Co genotype or a Ben Hill Co, GA genotype. Clone B is for sure one or the other.

The hybrid vigor in the offspring suggests these two clones are not siblings.

posts.body_html:
this cross is such a great performer! They're quite uniform: as young seedlings, I selected out 2 or 3 of the very best individuals, but now that they've all reached maturity and have been grown out for many years now, it's hard to tell one clone from the other! They all grow fast, have great vigor overall, very similar shape, near identical colors(if there are differences, it's typically environmental), produce well defined red throats under optimal conditions, and are for sure some of the easiest plants in the collection to grow!

Here's an updated pic for you guys to see: The two open traps in the foreground, left is AxB clone#1 and the rest of the traps to the right are AxB clone#2! While I would offer a dollar to anyone who can distinguish the two clones from each other (don't all rush in at once!), I don't think such an offer is necessary since for all intents and purposes, both clones are nearly identical:
